articles.title: I Am a Peaceful Soul: What That Actually Means
articles.titleHinglish: Main Ek Shaant Aatma Hoon: Iska Matlab Kya Hai
articles.content:
The sentence is repeated so often in spiritual circles that it has become wallpaper. Said without understanding, it is just a pleasant phrase. Said with understanding, it is one of the most practical tools available for an ordinary difficult day.

Start with what it is not. It is not a claim that you are always calm. Anyone who has sat in traffic knows otherwise. It is not a denial that you have a body, a job, a family and a temper.

What it points at is a distinction between what you are and what you are currently carrying.

Through the day you wear roles — employee, son, daughter, senior, customer, driver. Each comes with expectations and a mood attached. The trouble begins when the role stops being something you are doing and becomes what you think you are. Then a bad review is not feedback about work; it is an attack on your existence. A rejection is not one person's decision; it is a statement about your value. The role and the self have merged, and every ordinary event now lands with maximum force.

Soul consciousness is the practice of separating them again. Not by pretending the roles do not matter — they do, and you should do them well — but by remembering that the one performing them is not made of them. In this framing, peace is not something you achieve at the end of a long effort. It is your original condition, temporarily covered by whatever the day has stacked on top of it.

What does this look like in practice, on a Tuesday?

Before entering a difficult room, take ten seconds and say it internally, with attention: I am a peaceful soul. Not as a chant — as a reminder of who is walking in.

When criticism lands, notice the gap. They are describing my work. My work is something I did. I am the one who did it and can do it better. Small distinction, enormous difference in how much it hurts.

And when you look at a difficult person, try seeing the same distinction in them. The rude clerk is also a soul wearing a bad day and a role they may hate. This is not sentiment; it is the fastest available way to stop taking a stranger's behaviour personally.

One honest limit, since this journal does not overclaim. This practice will not make you unaffected. Grief will still arrive, anger will still rise, and someone who says otherwise after six months of meditation is performing. What it does is smaller and real: it puts a small distance between the event and your identity, and in that distance you get to choose your response. That distance is most of what anyone means by peace.
articles.contentHinglish:
Yeh line aadhyatmik duniya mein itni baar dohrayi jaati hai ki deewar ka wallpaper ban gayi hai. Bina samjhe boli jaaye to bas ek pyaari si baat hai. Samajh ke boli jaaye to yeh ek aam mushkil din ke liye sabse practical auzaaron mein se ek hai.

Pehle yeh ki wo hai kya nahi. Yeh dava nahi hai ki aap hamesha shaant ho. Traffic mein baithe kisi bhi insaan ko pata hai ki aisa nahi hai. Yeh inkaar bhi nahi hai ki aapka sharir, job, parivaar aur gussa hai.

Yeh jis cheez ki taraf ishaara karti hai wo hai — aap kya ho aur is waqt kya uthaye hue ho, in dono ka farq.

Din bhar aap kirdaar pehente ho — karmchari, beta, beti, senior, customer, driver. Har ek ke saath ummeedein aati hain aur ek mood juda hota hai. Dikkat tab shuru hoti hai jab kirdaar aapka kiya hua kaam nahi rehta aur aapki pehchaan ban jaata hai. Tab buri review kaam par feedback nahi rehti; wo aapke hone par hamla ban jaati hai. Ek rejection ek insaan ka faisla nahi rehta; wo aapki keemat ka bayaan ban jaata hai. Kirdaar aur khud ek ho gaye, aur ab har aam ghatna poori taakat se lagti hai.

Aatma-abhimani hona inhe dobara alag karne ki practice hai. Kirdaaron ko bekaar samajh kar nahi — wo mayne rakhte hain aur unhe achhe se karna chahiye — balki yeh yaad rakh kar ki jo unhe nibha raha hai wo unse bana hua nahi hai. Is nazariye mein shanti wo cheez nahi jo lambi mehnat ke ant mein milti hai. Wo aapki asli halat hai, jispar din ne jo bhi laada hai wo kuch der ke liye chadha hua hai.

Mangalvaar ko yeh practically dikhta kaisa hai?

Kisi mushkil kamre mein ghusne se pehle dus second ruk kar, dhyan se, andar bolo: main ek shaant aatma hoon. Mantra ki tarah nahi — yeh yaad dilane ke liye ki andar ja kaun raha hai.

Jab criticism aaye, gap dekho. Wo mere kaam ka varnan kar rahe hain. Kaam wo hai jo maine kiya. Karne wala main hoon, aur behtar bhi kar sakta hoon. Chhota sa farq, aur chubhan mein bahut bada antar.

Aur jab kisi mushkil insaan ko dekho to wahi farq unme bhi dekhne ki koshish karo. Rukha clerk bhi ek aatma hai jo ek kharab din aur shayad ek napasand kirdaar pehne hue hai. Yeh bhavukta nahi hai; kisi ajnabi ke behaviour ko dil par lena band karne ka yeh sabse tez raasta hai.

Ek imaandaar limit, kyunki yeh journal zyada dava nahi karta. Is practice se aap achhoote nahi ho jaayenge. Gham phir bhi aayega, gussa phir bhi uthega, aur chhe mahine meditation ke baad jo ulta kehta hai wo performance kar raha hai. Jo hota hai wo chhota aur asli hai: ghatna aur aapki pehchaan ke beech thodi si doori aa jaati hai, aur usi doori mein aap apna jawab chun paate ho. Shanti se log zyadatar wahi doori hi samajhte hain.

articles.title: You Are Not Your Thoughts, You Are the One Watching Them
articles.titleHinglish: Aap Apne Vichaar Nahi Ho, Aap Unhe Dekhne Wale Ho
articles.content:
Sit quietly for one minute and try to have no thoughts. You will fail, and the failure is the most useful thing here. Notice who noticed. A thought arrived, and something observed it arriving. That observer is not the thought.

This is not philosophy for its own sake. It is the whole basis of not being dragged around by your own mind.

Most suffering has a specific structure. A thought appears — I am not good enough, they are ignoring me, this will go badly — and rather than being seen as a thought, it is experienced as a report on reality. Once accepted as a report, the body responds accordingly and the day is shaped by it.

The practice is to insert one word. Not I am useless, but: there is a thought that I am useless. The content is unchanged and its authority collapses. You are no longer inside the sentence; you are looking at it.

Some people find it easier with an image. Thoughts as trains arriving at a platform: you can watch them come and go without boarding every one. Or the traditional version — the sky and the clouds. The clouds are dramatic, sometimes for days, and none of them do any lasting damage to the sky.

A few practical notes for when you try this.

Do not fight the thought. Argument feeds it. You do not have to disprove I am useless — proving it wrong keeps you engaged with it. Simply see it and let it pass, and it dissolves faster than any counter-argument would achieve.

Expect to forget. You will notice the thought, apply the distance, and then twenty minutes later find yourself fully inside another one. That is not failure; that is the exercise. The noticing is the repetition, and the repetitions are what build the capacity.

And be careful not to turn this into suppression. Watching a thought is not the same as refusing to feel it. Grief, anger, fear — you can observe them and feel them at the same time, and observing them without being commanded by them is precisely the aim.

The old texts put it as the difference between the mind and the one who has a mind. It sounds abstract until the first time it works on you — a familiar cruel thought arrives, you see it as a thought, and it goes past without taking the day with it. After that, no one needs to convince you.
articles.contentHinglish:
Ek minute chup baith kar koshish karo ki koi vichaar na aaye. Aap fail hoge, aur wahi fail hona yahan sabse kaam ki cheez hai. Dhyan do ki notice kisne kiya. Ek vichaar aaya, aur kisi ne use aate hue dekha. Wo dekhne wala vichaar nahi hai.

Yeh sirf philosophy ke liye philosophy nahi hai. Apne hi dimaag ke peechhe ghaseete jaane se bachne ka poora aadhaar yahi hai.

Zyadatar dukh ki ek khaas banawat hoti hai. Ek vichaar aata hai — main kaafi achha nahi hoon, wo mujhe ignore kar rahe hain, yeh bura hi jaayega — aur use vichaar ki tarah dekhne ki jagah haqeeqat ki report ki tarah jiya jaata hai. Ek baar report maan liya, to sharir uske hisaab se react karta hai aur poora din uske aakaar mein dhal jaata hai.

Practice yeh hai ki ek shabd ghusa do. "Main bekaar hoon" nahi, balki: "ek vichaar aaya hai ki main bekaar hoon". Baat wahi hai aur uska rutba gir jaata hai. Ab aap us sentence ke andar nahi ho; aap use dekh rahe ho.

Kuch logon ko image se aasaan lagta hai. Vichaar platform par aati hui trainein hain: aap unhe aate jaate dekh sakte ho bina har ek mein chadhe. Ya paramparik version — aasmaan aur baadal. Baadal dramatic hote hain, kabhi kabhi kai din tak, aur unme se koi bhi aasmaan ko sthayi nuksaan nahi pahunchata.

Karte waqt kuch practical baatein.

Vichaar se lado mat. Bahas use khaana deti hai. Aapko "main bekaar hoon" ko galat sabit karna zaroori nahi — galat sabit karna aapko usi se jode rakhta hai. Bas dekho aur guzar jaane do, wo kisi bhi jawabi dalil se jaldi ghul jaata hai.

Bhool jaane ki ummeed rakho. Aap vichaar ko notice karoge, doori banaoge, aur bees minute baad khud ko kisi doosre ke poore andar paoge. Yeh asafalta nahi hai; yahi exercise hai. Notice karna hi dohraav hai, aur dohraav se hi kshamta banti hai.

Aur dhyan rakho ki yeh dabaana na ban jaaye. Vichaar ko dekhna aur use mehsoos karne se inkaar karna — do alag cheezein hain. Gham, gussa, dar — inhe aap ek saath dekh bhi sakte ho aur mehsoos bhi kar sakte ho, aur inhe bina unka hukum maane dekhna hi asli maqsad hai.

Purane granth ise mann aur mann wale ke farq ki tarah kehte hain. Sunne mein abstract lagta hai — jab tak pehli baar yeh aap par kaam na kare. Ek jaana-pehchaana kadwa vichaar aata hai, aap use vichaar ki tarah dekhte ho, aur wo poora din apne saath liye bina nikal jaata hai. Uske baad kisi ko aapko samjhane ki zaroorat nahi rehti.

articles.title: Drishti: What Changes When You Change How You Look
articles.titleHinglish: Drishti: Dekhne Ka Tareeka Badalne Se Kya Badalta Hai
articles.content:
There is an old idea in this tradition that is easy to dismiss as sentimental and turns out to be extremely practical: as your vision, so your world. Drishti — the way you look at someone — decides most of what happens next between you.

Think about how you see a specific person you find difficult. A colleague, a relative, a neighbour. By now you have compressed them into a summary — lazy, arrogant, manipulative, cold. That summary is efficient. It is also a filter, and from now on you will notice mainly the behaviour that confirms it. This is not weakness of character; it is how attention works. Once a person is categorised, the mind stops collecting new evidence.

And they can feel it. People know when they have been written off, even when nothing is said. Then they behave worse with you than with others, and you take that as final proof, and the loop is complete. Two people can lock each other into their worst versions for years without a single open argument.

The practice is to look at the person underneath the behaviour. Not to excuse it — a rude person is still being rude, and you still hold your boundary. But to hold, at the same time, a second fact: this is someone carrying something you cannot see.

The practical version is short. Before an encounter you are dreading, take ten seconds and see them as a soul rather than a summary. Someone with a history, a fear, a pressure at home. Then behave normally.

What is surprising is how often the other person's behaviour changes without a word being spoken about any of this. Some of that is them responding to a softer face. Most of it is you — you stop scanning for the offence, so you find fewer of them, and you stop delivering the small cold signals you did not know you were sending.

And there is a version of this to turn on yourself, which is harder. Most people look at themselves with the same reduced summary — lazy, failure, always like this. That vision produces exactly the same effect: filtered evidence, a self-fulfilling prophecy, and a person who behaves worse in their own presence than they would with a friend.

One warning against misuse. Soft vision does not mean staying in a room where you are being harmed. You can see someone as a soul and still not let them near your life. The tradition never asked anyone to be a doormat; it asked that you not add hatred to a situation that already has enough weight in it.
articles.contentHinglish:
Is parampara mein ek purani baat hai jise bhavuk keh kar hataana aasaan hai aur jo asal mein bahut practical nikalti hai: jaisi drishti, waisi srishti. Drishti — aap kisi ko dekhte kaise ho — yahi zyadatar tay karti hai ki aapke beech aage kya hoga.

Socho ki aap us ek insaan ko kaise dekhte ho jo aapko mushkil lagta hai. Koi colleague, rishtedaar, padosi. Ab tak aap unhe ek summary mein daba chuke ho — aalsi, ghamandi, chalak, thanda. Wo summary kaam ki hai. Wo ek filter bhi hai, aur ab se aap zyadatar wahi behaviour notice karoge jo use sahi sabit kare. Yeh charitra ki kamzori nahi hai; dhyan aise hi kaam karta hai. Ek baar insaan ko category mil gayi, dimaag naya saboot jama karna band kar deta hai.

Aur unhe mehsoos hota hai. Logon ko pata chal jaata hai ki unhe likh kar chhod diya gaya hai, chahe kuch bola na gaya ho. Phir wo aapke saath doosron se bura behave karte hain, aur aap use aakhri saboot maan lete ho, aur loop poora ho jaata hai. Do log ek doosre ko unke sabse bure version mein saalon tak band rakh sakte hain, bina ek khuli ladai ke.

Practice yeh hai ki behaviour ke neeche wale insaan ko dekho. Use maaf karne ke liye nahi — rukha insaan ab bhi rukha hai, aur aap apni boundary bhi rakhoge. Par saath hi ek doosra fact bhi pakde raho: yeh koi hai jo aisa kuch utha raha hai jo aapko dikhta nahi.

Practical version chhota hai. Jis mulaqat se dar lag raha hai, usse pehle dus second lo aur unhe summary ki jagah ek aatma ki tarah dekho. Koi jiska ateet hai, koi dar hai, ghar ka koi dabaav hai. Phir normal behave karo.

Hairani ki baat yeh hai ki aksar saamne wale ka behaviour bina ek shabd bole badal jaata hai. Uska kuch hissa yeh hai ki wo narm chehre ko jawab de rahe hain. Zyadatar hissa aap ho — aap chot dhoondhna band kar dete ho, isliye kam milti hai, aur wo chhote thande signal bhejna band kar dete ho jo aapko pata bhi nahi tha ki aap bhej rahe the.

Aur iska ek version khud par bhi lagana hai, jo zyada mushkil hai. Zyadatar log khud ko bhi usi kati-chhanti summary se dekhte hain — aalsi, fail, hamesha aisa hi. Us drishti ka asar bilkul wahi hota hai: chhana hua saboot, khud ko sach karti bhavishyavani, aur ek insaan jo apne hi saath waise behave karta hai jaise kisi dost ke saath kabhi nahi karta.

Galat istemaal ke khilaf ek chetavani. Narm drishti ka matlab us kamre mein rukna nahi hai jahan aapko chot pahunchayi ja rahi ho. Aap kisi ko aatma ki tarah dekh sakte ho aur phir bhi use apni zindagi ke paas na aane do. Parampara ne kabhi kisi se paidaan banne ko nahi kaha; usne itna kaha ki jis sthiti mein pehle hi kaafi bojh hai usme nafrat mat jodo.
